title: Text, Reader, and Interpretation
text:
Formalist critics once insisted that a literary work should be read as a self-contained object, its meaning residing in the interplay of language, structure and imagery rather than in the biography of its author. Later theorists, however, challenged this autonomy, arguing that every reading is shaped by the historical and ideological assumptions of its reader. Reception theory, for instance, held that a text acquires meaning only when it is actualised by an interpreter.

Such arguments have not simply displaced earlier methods; rather, they have produced a more cautious criticism that acknowledges its own presuppositions. A critic who explicates a novel's imagery today is generally aware that the choice of vocabulary is itself an interpretive act. The tension between text and reader therefore remains productive, sustaining debate rather than resolving it.

questions.text: According to the first paragraph, what did Formalist critics insist on?
options: that a work should be read in light of its author's biography
that a work should be read as a self-contained object
that every reading is shaped by the reader's ideology
that a text acquires meaning only through an interpreter

questions.text: According to the second paragraph, what is a critic who explicates a novel's imagery today generally aware of?
options: that imagery has no place in modern criticism
that the reader's biography determines the meaning
that the choice of vocabulary is an interpretive act
that earlier methods have completely resolved the debate

questions.text: What can be inferred about the author's view of earlier critical methods?
options: They have been completely rejected by modern critics.
They have been partly absorbed into a more cautious approach.
They were based on the reader's personal experience alone.
They never considered the relationship between text and reader.

questions.text: Why does the author describe the tension between text and reader as productive?
options: Because it allows critics to reach a single final verdict.
Because it removes the need for interpretation.
Because it keeps the debate open rather than settling it.
Because it shows that the author's intentions are decisive.

vocabulary.definition: the condition of being independent from outside influence
made real or brought into effect through action
assumptions taken for granted before an argument begins
explains something in detail so that its meaning becomes clear

paragraph_translations: Формалістичні критики колись наполягали на тому, що літературний твір слід читати як самодостатній об'єкт, а його значення полягає у взаємодії мови, структури й образності, а не в біографії автора. Однак пізніші теоретики поставили під сумнів цю автономність, стверджуючи, що кожне прочитання формується історичними та ідеологічними припущеннями читача. Наприклад, теорія рецепції вважала, що текст набуває значення лише тоді, коли його актуалізує інтерпретатор.

Такі аргументи не просто витіснили попередні методи; радше вони породили більш обережну критику, яка визнає власні передумови. Критик, який сьогодні пояснює образність роману, як правило, усвідомлює, що вибір слів сам по собі є інтерпретаційним актом. Тому напруження між текстом і читачем залишається продуктивним, підтримуючи дискусію, а не вирішуючи її.
